Motorcycle Security on Tour

Having your motorcycle stolen or damaged mid-tour is every tourer's nightmare. While the UK is generally safe for motorcycle touring, opportunistic theft happens, and a few simple precautions drastically reduce your risk.

Locks and Physical Security

Layers of security work best. Each additional lock adds time and difficulty for a thief:

  • Disc lock: Minimum security. Small, lightweight, fits in a jacket pocket. Use a bright-coloured reminder cable to prevent riding off with it attached.
  • Chain lock: A 1-1.5m chain through the wheel and around a fixed point (railing, post, ground anchor). Heavier to carry but much more secure. Almax and Pragmasis make motorcycle-specific chains.
  • Grip lock: Locks the throttle and brake lever together. A visible deterrent and easy to carry.
  • Steering lock: Use your bike's built-in steering lock every time you park. It's the easiest security measure and costs nothing.

Parking Strategies

  • In sight: Whenever possible, park where you can see your bike — outside the café window, by the pub garden, visible from your B&B room.
  • Against a wall: Park with one side against a wall. This makes it harder to lift and limits access points.
  • Among other bikes: If there are other motorcycles parked, group together. Thieves are less likely to target a row of bikes than a lone one.
  • Well-lit areas: At night, park under street lights or in a lit car park. Darkness is a thief's friend.
  • Motorcycle parking bays: Many UK towns have designated motorcycle bays, often free. These are usually in prominent locations and sometimes have ground anchors.

Overnight Security

This is when your bike is most vulnerable. Reduce risk with these habits:

  • Ask your B&B or hotel about secure parking — a garage or gated area is ideal.
  • At campsites, park your bike beside your tent where you can hear any disturbance.
  • Use a disc lock and steering lock at minimum every night.
  • A motorcycle cover hides what's underneath and adds another layer of deterrent.
  • Remove or lock your helmet and any detachable luggage.
Most motorcycle theft is opportunistic. Make your bike slightly harder to steal than the one next to it and you've dramatically reduced your risk. Every layer of security — even a simple disc lock — makes a difference.

Electronic Security

  • GPS tracker: A hidden GPS tracker (Monimoto, Datatool) sends an alert to your phone if your bike is moved. Won't prevent theft but massively improves recovery chances.
  • Alarm: Aftermarket alarms are visible deterrents. A loud alarm in a quiet village will attract attention quickly.
  • AirTag or SmartTag: A cheap, lightweight tracking option. Hide one in your bike's bodywork or under the seat.

Helmet and Gear Security

  • Use a helmet lock cable or carabiner to secure your helmet to the bike when you're away from it.
  • Don't leave expensive gear visibly in unlocked luggage — take it with you or lock it inside your panniers.
  • At attractions and viewpoints, take your tank bag (with wallet, phone, camera) with you. Never leave valuables visible.

Insurance and Documentation

If the worst happens:

  • Report theft to police immediately (call 101, or 999 if it's happening)
  • Get a crime reference number
  • Contact your insurer within 24 hours
  • Having photos of your bike and recording the VIN/frame number speeds up the process

Security is about making your bike an unattractive target. A few pounds worth of locks and a couple of minutes of parking awareness keep your touring companion safe and your trip on track.
keyTakeaways: Layer your security: a disc lock, chain lock and the steering lock together deter opportunists.
Park in sight, against a wall, among other bikes and in well-lit areas or dedicated motorcycle bays.
A GPS tracker or hidden AirTag/SmartTag helps recover a stolen bike; an alarm deters casual theft.
Use a cover overnight so thieves cannot identify a valuable bike or see the lock setup.
Keep insurance and V5C details accessible and photograph your bike before the tour.

faq.q: What is the best lock for touring?
faq.a: No single lock is enough, so layer them. A compact disc lock stops the bike being rolled away and fits in a pocket for daytime stops. For overnight security add a chain lock secured to a solid anchor point to prevent the bike being lifted into a van. Always engage the steering lock as well, and a grip lock adds a quick deterrent for short stops.

faq.q: Where should I park my bike overnight on tour?
faq.a: Choose somewhere in sight of your accommodation if possible, against a wall to protect one side, and among other motorcycles where thieves are more likely to be noticed. Well-lit areas and dedicated motorcycle bays are ideal. Many biker-friendly pubs and B&Bs offer secure parking, so ask when booking.

Yes, for peace of mind and recovery. A hardwired GPS tracker or a hidden AirTag or Samsung SmartTag greatly improves the chance of recovering a stolen bike, and some insurers reduce premiums for approved trackers. Pair a tracker with an audible alarm, which deters casual thieves before they get far.

faq.q: Should I use a bike cover on tour?
faq.a: A cover is worthwhile overnight. It hides a valuable bike from casual view, conceals your lock setup so a thief cannot plan their approach, and protects the bike from overnight rain and dew. A lightweight packable cover takes up little luggage space and pays for itself in reduced worry and a dry seat in the morning.
